methodology_note: Static walk of the full source tree, read-only; nothing was built, restored or executed, and no runtime was observed. SCOPING RULE APPLIED: `git ls-files` returned 22 tracked files, and `git status --untracked-files=all` returned 31 untracked files under references/ (22 .md), assets/ (7), scripts/ (1) and fixtures/ (1). Those 31 are Discovery-skill reference/template material staged into the source root by the dispatch harness, not application source, and they are EXCLUDED from every count, module, and coupling finding in this document (see duplication_map). All 4 C# files, both .csproj files, the .sln, all 4 NuGet config files, app.config, build.bat and tasks.ps1 were read in full. Dependency edges were derived from MSBuild <Reference>/<Import> elements, packages.config entries, and `using`/qualified-type references in source; there is no reflection, DI container, dynamic dispatch or code generation in the tree, so the import graph is complete rather than best-effort. Absence claims are grep-derived, not assumed: a case-insensitive search of all tracked files for connectionstring|Data Source=|Initial Catalog|SqlConnection|OleDb|Odbc|EntityFramework|System.Data.SqlClient|HttpClient|WebRequest|Soap|WCF|ServiceModel|Authenticate|Login|Identity|Principal|appSettings|ConfigurationManager|Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable returned ZERO matches, and a search for <ProjectReference> returned zero matches. FAN-OUT DECISION: not fanned out. The skill's rule fans out above 8 top-level modules / 50 KLOC / 20 tables; this tree has 2 modules, 172 lines of C# and 0 tables, so a single-pass walk is faster than sub-agent coordination. WHAT THE WALK COULD NOT REACH: the restored `packages/` directory does not exist in the workspace, so psake.net's Functions.psm1 (which supplies Get-DefaultPropertiesFile and Import-DefaultTasks, referenced at tasks.ps1:5 and tasks.ps1:11) was NOT read - the concrete Clean/Build/Test/Version task bodies are out-of-repo and unverified. No db-schema.json was written because the application has no database; manufacturing an empty schema file would assert a walk that found nothing had found a schema. The sibling Discovery artifacts declared for this pass (sqlserver-object-inventory, language-detection, db-archaeology, data-flow-trace, identity-landscape, tiff-corpus-assessment) are produced by their own skills in their own dispatches and are not emitted here; for this application most are inapplicable on the evidence above.

major_components.name: Program.Main (console entry point)
major_components.responsibility: The application's only invocation surface: writes a banner to stdout, seeds a hard-coded six-item in-memory inventory, calls UpdateQuality() exactly once, then blocks on a keypress and exits. Classified `ui` because it is the sole human-facing surface; it accepts no arguments (the `args` parameter is never read). Evidence: src/GildedRose.Console/Program.cs:8-35.

major_components.name: Program.UpdateQuality (inventory rules engine)
major_components.responsibility: The entire business logic of the application: 75 lines of nested conditionals that adjust each item's Quality and SellIn per item-specific rules, dispatching on item-name string literals. Evidence: src/GildedRose.Console/Program.cs:37-111.

major_components.name: Item (domain model)
major_components.responsibility: A three-property POCO (Name, SellIn, Quality) with public setters and no validation, invariants or persistence mapping. Declared in the same file and namespace as the entry point rather than in a separate assembly, which is why it is a `shared-library` in intent but not in packaging. Evidence: src/GildedRose.Console/Program.cs:115-122.

major_components.name: GildedRose.Tests (xUnit test assembly)
major_components.responsibility: A build-time-only library assembly holding one tautological test, Assert.True(true). It declares NO reference to GildedRose.Console, so it cannot exercise any production code. Kind is `unknown` rather than `shared-library` because a test harness is not a component of the running system and the closed vocabulary has no test-assembly value. Evidence: src/GildedRose.Tests/TestAssemblyTests.cs:7-11, src/GildedRose.Tests/GildedRose.Tests.csproj:42-58.

god_type_single_file_application.description: One 124-line file holds the process entry point, the seed data, the complete business-rules engine and the domain model, in one namespace, with the rules engine as an instance method on the class whose other job is hosting Main(). There is no layering to preserve and no seam to cut, so any decomposition begins by inventing boundaries that do not exist yet.

magic_string_dispatch.description: Every rule branch is selected by comparing Item.Name against a literal string - "Aged Brie", "Sulfuras, Hand of Ragnaros" and "Backstage passes to a TAFKAL80ETC concert" - 8 comparisons in total, several negated and nested inside each other (lines 85-91 nest three name comparisons four levels deep). Behaviour is coupled to exact data values with no enum, subtype or lookup, so renaming an inventory item silently changes its business rules, and the comparisons are case-sensitive and whitespace-sensitive with no normalisation.

test_assembly_not_wired_to_production_co.description: The solution contains a test project and a production project with NO edge between them: no <ProjectReference> exists anywhere in the repository, and the one test method asserts Assert.True(true). The coupling finding is the ABSENCE of a dependency that the solution's structure implies - a reader who counts two projects and an xUnit reference would reasonably assume coverage exists. It does not. Compounding it, UpdateQuality is an instance method on the internal class Program reading a private field, so the edge cannot simply be added; the rules must first be made reachable (public/extracted) before any test can call them.

shared_mutable_state_through_public_sett.description: Item exposes public setters on all three properties and holds no invariants, while UpdateQuality mutates the caller's objects in place via the list indexer. The documented invariants (Quality never negative, never above 50, Sulfuras fixed at 80) are enforced only by the conditionals inside this single loop, so any second writer - or any reordering of the loop - can violate them undetectably. The loop also reaches Items[i] repeatedly rather than binding a local, so a rule change must be applied consistently across ~25 indexer accesses.

deep_conditional_nesting.description: UpdateQuality reaches five levels of nested conditionals inside the loop (lines 83-95: SellIn<0, then three negated name comparisons, then Quality>0, then a fourth name comparison), and expresses one branch as the self-cancelling `Quality = Quality - Quality` rather than an assignment to zero. The rules a reader must recover are interleaved rather than separated per item type, which is why business-rule extraction downstream must read the whole method as one unit rather than per-branch.

build_chain_depends_on_out_of_repo_conve.description: The build is not self-describing or hermetic. tasks.ps1 defines no task bodies - it calls Get-DefaultPropertiesFile and Import-DefaultTasks Version, Clean, Build, Test, all supplied by the out-of-repo psake.net 0.1.3 package, so what Build and Test actually DO is invisible in this repository (and was unreadable in this walk, since packages/ is not restored). build.bat additionally downloads NuGet.exe from https://www.nuget.org over the network when absent and restores from the deprecated https://nuget.org/api/v2/ v2 feed, hard-requires cmd plus Windows PowerShell >= 3.0, and shells out to GitVersion.exe. Every one of those is a build-time dependency on something outside the repo, and the v2 feed plus an unpinned nuget.exe download is also a supply-chain exposure.

divergent_versioning_of_one_build.description: Three GitVersion components at three versions participate in one solution build - GitVersionTask 2.0.1 (console, declared but never imported), GitVersionTask 3.4.1 (tests, imported as a target), GitVersion.CommandLine 2.0.0 (invoked by build.bat) - and NUnit.Runners 2.6.4 is restored at solution level although no project references NUnit. The console assembly therefore ends up with the hard-coded AssemblyVersion 1.0.0.0 while the test assembly is version-stamped by GitVersion.

open_questions: The closed `kind` vocabulary has no value for an interactive console entry point. `unknown` was chosen deliberately: the run is batch-SHAPED (one pass over the whole inventory, then exit) but not unattended - it blocks on a keypress at src/GildedRose.Console/Program.cs:33, so it cannot be scheduled, and `batch`/`scheduled-job` would both assert a capability this application does not have. Forcing `ui-page` would be equally wrong - there is no page.

Section 508 / WCAG 2.1 AA applicability is UNDETERMINED for this surface. The interface is human-facing, which normally triggers the obligation, but WCAG success criteria are written for web content and there is no page, form or report here - only a single stdout line ('OMGHAI!') and a keypress wait. A 508 determination for a character-mode console surface needs the accessibility reviewer's ruling, not this walk's guess.

No machine-facing interface exists: zero HTTP endpoints, zero SOAP/WCF service contracts, zero queue consumers or producers, zero file imports or exports, and zero outbound calls (greps for HttpClient, WebRequest, ServiceModel, Soap and WCF over all tracked files returned nothing). Confirm whether the real production system is fed by an upstream interface that this repository does not contain.

recommended_decomposition_boundaries.note: CUT FIRST, and cut inside the module rather than between modules. Extract Item plus the per-item-type rules out of Program into a separately-referencable library with a public entry point (e.g. IItemUpdateRule per item category, replacing the 8 name-literal comparisons at Program.cs:41-91 with polymorphic or table-driven dispatch). This is the only boundary that unblocks the others: while the rules live on an internal class's instance method reading a private field (Program.cs:5,7,37), nothing outside the assembly - test, service or replacement - can call them. Downstream lines should treat 'the rules engine' as this proposed boundary, NOT as an existing module, because today it is 75 lines inside the entry-point type.

What remains of Program after the extraction: composition, seed-data acquisition and invocation. Two structural facts must change here for any target-state deployment on the FAA profile's substrate (Amazon ECS on Fargate, profiles/faa/config/common.yaml cloud_container_service): the blocking System.Console.ReadKey() at Program.cs:33 makes the process non-terminating under an orchestrator, and the six hard-coded items at Program.cs:16-26 make the run non-parameterisable. Both are host concerns, not domain concerns, which is why they belong on this side of the cut.

Re-point the orphaned test assembly at the extracted domain library with a real <ProjectReference> and replace Assert.True(true) with characterisation tests pinning today's OBSERVED behaviour (including the Conjured gap and the `Quality = Quality - Quality` branch at Program.cs:99) BEFORE any refactor. The behavioural baseline does not exist yet, so any downstream transformation of this application is currently unverifiable - this boundary is a precondition for the other two, not a follow-up.

STATED EXPLICITLY so a downstream line does not read the boundaries above as a microservice plan. At 172 lines, one deployable, zero endpoints, zero integrations and zero tables, there is no service to split out and no shared database to disentangle; the coupling findings here are intra-assembly design debt. Portfolio-level treatment (retain / rationalise / retire) is the disposition line's call and depends on resolving whether this application_id maps to a real FAA system at all - see open_questions.

UNIMPLEMENTED DOCUMENTED RULE: README.md states that '"Conjured" items degrade in Quality twice as fast as normal items', and Program.cs:26 seeds a 'Conjured Mana Cake' - but UpdateQuality contains NO branch matching 'Conjured' (the string appears nowhere in the rules at Program.cs:37-111), so conjured items currently degrade at the normal single rate. Is this the kata's intended starting state (the exercise to be completed), or a real production defect to be carried into the target state as a known behaviour? The answer changes whether business-rule extraction should record the rule as specified-but-absent or as out of scope.

The 75-line UpdateQuality method is the application's entire business logic and has ZERO test coverage (src/GildedRose.Tests/TestAssemblyTests.cs:7-11 asserts Assert.True(true) and the test project references no production code). Before any transformation, who owns sign-off on the characterisation tests that will define correct behaviour - particularly for the `Quality = Quality - Quality` branch at Program.cs:99 and whether the 50-Quality cap is intended to apply to the second and third backstage-pass increments at Program.cs:61-71?
